chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Amr ibn Uthman from al-Mufaddal and from Zayd al-Shahham, all from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the crescents, so he said:
"They are the crescents of the months. So when you see the crescent, fast, and when you see it, break your fast."

I said: Do you see if the month is twenty-nine days, should I make up that day? He said: "No, unless two just witnesses testify for you. If they testify that they saw the crescent before that, then make up that day."

key_terms.الْأَهِلَّةُ: Crescents (plural of hilal, referring to the new moon)
key_terms.الْهِلاَلُ: The crescent (specifically the new moon marking the start of a month)
key_terms.تَقْضِي: Make up (a missed day of fasting)

ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence determine the start and end of Ramadan based on moon sighting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the lunar crescent sighting as the primary determinant for the start and end of fasting, emphasizing the practical necessity of witness testimony to validate an extended twenty-nine-day month. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential reliance on empirical evidence (bayyina) from just witnesses to resolve discrepancies in the lunar calendar, ensuring the integrity of the fasting period.
